reading.body:
Hakeem Jeffries took $30,500 in PAC money from eight AI companies and voted Yea on four AI-related bills, with no recorded vote against one.

The money is the denser signal. Eight contributions between June 2025 and August 2026, from Intel, Amazon, Meta, Microsoft, Oracle, and Google committees, ranging from $2,500 to $5,000. Amazon gave twice. Microsoft and Oracle each gave twice. The four recorded votes all passed on suspension of the rules, a procedure used for broadly uncontroversial measures, so none of them shows a contested position on AI.

For AI specifically, this is the financial plumbing that sits upstream of any compute or data center policy. The companies funding these committees are the same ones building and buying the compute, and the grid constraints on that compute are ultimately resolved through legislation and regulatory choices made by people who take this money. The record does not show how Jeffries voted on any bill that divided the parties, because the data contains no such vote.

What the data does not cover: no sponsored bills, only votes. No amounts from individuals, only committees. No dates on the four news stories beyond their publication, and no indication of what the stories say about him. The record is a ledger of contributions and floor votes, not a measure of influence, and it draws no conclusion about motives.

summary: Every dated AI event this site holds for Hakeem Jeffries: bills sponsored or cosponsored, recorded votes on AI bills, and money from AI company and AI-focused political committees, newest first. 13 events, and 4 news stories that name them.
